revision_reason: Address review feedback: plan claimed Option F (Shell Command Timeout Wrapper) but had no implementation tasks. This revision adds a dedicated implementation phase for the timeout mechanism with concrete tasks, incorporates risk analyst feedback (120s default, hard-block completion signal, divergence detection), and provides detailed investigation of Claude Code's Bash tool invocation path to ensure the timeout wrapper is effective.
title: Architecture analysis: Fix refine phase push failures from branch history contamination, runaway shell commands, and wrong-branch completion signals
summary: The refine agent for issue #805 hung for 26+ minutes due to three cascading failures: (1) push denied because the shared pipeline branch included files from prior phases that the refine phase cannot modify, (2) a runaway `grep -rn / ...` command that searched the entire filesystem for 22+ minutes, and (3) the agent improvised a push to an unexpected branch name while the orchestrator accepted the completion signal without verifying commits on the expected branch. The recommended approach combines: pre-phase worktree sync in the orchestrator (Option B), agent prompt guardrails (Option E), a per-command timeout wrapper in the sandbox (Option F), gateway push-target enforcement (Option I), and completion signal branch verification (Option H). **Revision 2 adds explicit implementation tasks for Option F (the timeout wrapper)**, addressing reviewer feedback that the prior plan claimed Option F but had no tasks for it.

review_feedback_addressed.feedback: The plan summary claims to implement 'Option B + E + F + I + H from the analysis' but Option F (Shell Command Timeout Wrapper) has no implementation tasks. The analysis recommended E+F together as a defense-in-depth pair: prompt guardrails (soft) + command timeout (hard). Without Option F, the only protection against runaway commands is the prompt guardrail — which the plan's own risk table acknowledges as 'Med' likelihood of being ignored by the model.
review_feedback_addressed.resolution: Added a dedicated implementation phase (phase-3 in this revision) for Option F with three concrete tasks: (1) investigate Claude Code's Bash tool timeout behavior in the sandbox, (2) implement a system-level timeout wrapper, and (3) add prompt documentation about the timeout. The timeout implementation is now fully specified with acceptance criteria, affected files, and a concrete approach informed by codebase research.
review_feedback_addressed.key_finding: Investigation revealed that Claude Code's Bash tool already has a default 2-minute (120000ms) timeout per command, configurable up to 600000ms (10 minutes) per call. The 22-minute runaway grep in the incident suggests either the model explicitly set a higher timeout, the version used did not enforce the default, or the timeout was not applied in the sandbox's execution mode. The implementation must verify this behavior and add a system-level backup regardless.

problem_statement.description: During a pipeline run for issue #805, the refine agent was unable to push its analysis draft because the shared branch (egg/issue-805/work) contained accumulated commits from prior phases (plan drafts, implement results) that the refine phase's file restrictions reject. The agent then ran a `grep -rn 'Contract for issue' /` that searched the entire container filesystem at 100% CPU for 22+ minutes. It also improvised a push to a different branch name (egg/issue-805-refine), and signaled completion — which the orchestrator accepted without verifying the commit was on the expected branch. Net impact: 26-minute container hang, $8.23 wasted, pipeline in ambiguous state.

root_causes.title: Branch history contamination causes push denial
root_causes.description: All phases in a pipeline share a single branch (egg/{pipeline_id}/work) and worktree. The gateway's get_changed_files_in_push() computes `git diff --name-only origin/{branch}..HEAD`, which includes ALL files changed since the remote branch tip — including files committed by prior phases. If the remote branch hasn't been updated to include those commits, the diff includes prior-phase files that the current phase cannot modify, causing a push denial.

root_causes.title: No guardrails on unbounded filesystem searches
root_causes.description: The sandbox has no per-command timeout, no path-scope restriction, and no command filtering for shell operations. Claude Code's Bash tool has a per-call timeout parameter (default 120000ms, max 600000ms), but the model can set it higher and there is no system-level enforcement independent of Claude Code. A single `grep -rn / ...` or `find / ...` can consume 100% CPU for the entire session duration if the model sets a high timeout or the default is not enforced.
root_causes.location: sandbox/llm/claude/runner.py (session-level timeout only), Claude Code Bash tool (per-call timeout, model-controlled)

root_causes.title: Completion signal accepted without branch validation
root_causes.description: When the orchestrator receives egg-orch signal complete, it accepts the commit SHA as-is without verifying that new commits exist on the expected branch (pipeline.branch). The agent pushed to egg/issue-805-refine instead of egg/issue-805/work, signaled complete, and the pipeline continued with stale state on the expected branch.

current_architecture.push_validation_flow: The gateway's git_push() endpoint validates pushes in order: path validation -> remote resolution -> branch ownership (egg/ prefix) -> private repo mode -> role-based file restrictions -> agent-role restrictions -> phase-based file restrictions. Phase restrictions use get_changed_files_in_push() which diffs origin/{branch}..HEAD (two-dot), falling back to origin/main..HEAD if the remote branch doesn't exist.
current_architecture.branch_lifecycle: Pipelines use a single branch (egg/{pipeline_id}/work) across all phases. The orchestrator's _sync_worktree_with_remote() fetches and resets the worktree before each phase. If local is behind remote, it resets. If local is ahead (has unpushed commits), it skips the reset — this is the gap that causes the push denial when prior-phase commits haven't been pushed or fetched correctly.
current_architecture.shell_execution: In interactive mode, Claude Code is launched via os.execvpe() (sandbox/llm/runner.py:42). In headless mode, via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec() (sandbox/llm/claude/runner.py:304). Claude Code's Bash tool executes commands through its own internal subprocess mechanism — NOT through login shells. This means /etc/profile.d/ scripts, .bashrc, and .profile are NOT sourced for Bash tool commands. Git and gh commands are wrapped via sandbox/scripts/git and sandbox/scripts/gh to route through the gateway. No other commands have wrappers, timeouts, or path restrictions at the system level.
current_architecture.completion_signal: egg-orch signal complete sends an HTTP POST to /pipelines/{id}/signal. The orchestrator records the commit SHA in the contract state but does not verify it exists on the expected branch. The completion is accepted as long as the pipeline_id and agent_role are valid.

key_components.description: Checks if files are allowed for the current phase. Refine phase allows: .egg-state/contracts/*, .egg-state/drafts/*analysis*, .egg-state/checkpoints/*, .egg-state/agent-outputs/*, .egg-state/reviews/*.

key_components.name: _sync_worktree_with_remote()
key_components.description: Syncs the worktree before spawning a new phase's agent. Fetches remote and resets if local is behind. Skips reset if local is ahead of remote.

key_components.name: handle_complete_signal()
key_components.description: Processes agent completion signals. Accepts commit SHA without branch validation. Records in contract state and checks if all agents are complete.

key_components.name: auto_commit_worktree()

approaches.title: Pre-Phase Worktree Sync + Gateway Push-Target Enforcement + Sandbox Timeout + Prompt Guardrails (Recommended)
approaches.description: A combined approach addressing all three root causes with targeted fixes at the appropriate layer. (1) Ensure _sync_worktree_with_remote() pushes accumulated commits before spawning the next phase agent. (2) Add gateway enforcement that pipeline agents can only push to the session's expected branch. (3) Add a per-command timeout wrapper in the sandbox. (4) Add prompt guardrails warning against root-level filesystem searches. (5) Add completion signal branch verification.

orchestrator_sync.change: In _sync_worktree_with_remote(), when local is ahead of remote, check the prior phase's agent execution status. If the prior phase completed successfully, push those commits to the remote branch BEFORE resetting. If the prior phase failed/was killed, reset to remote (discard incomplete work). Handle divergence (ahead AND behind) by attempting fast-forward merge; signal pipeline error if merge fails.

sandbox_timeout.change: Implement a system-level per-command timeout independent of Claude Code's Bash tool timeout parameter. The approach: (1) verify Claude Code's default Bash timeout is active and not overridden, (2) add a backup system-level timeout via a shell wrapper that enforces BASH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT (default 120s) using the `timeout` coreutil, (3) install the wrapper in a way that covers Claude Code's subprocess invocation path. This provides defense-in-depth: even if the model overrides Claude Code's per-call timeout to 600s, the system-level wrapper caps total execution time.

recommended_approach.title: Pre-Phase Worktree Sync + Gateway Push-Target Enforcement + Sandbox Timeout + Prompt Guardrails + Completion Signal Verification
recommended_approach.justification: This issue has three independent root causes that each require a fix at the appropriate layer. Approach A is the only option that addresses all three. The pre-phase sync (RC-1 fix) is the safest solution because it preserves the gateway's conservative two-dot diff unchanged. The gateway push-target enforcement (RC-3 fix) is a natural extension of existing pipeline-mode restrictions. The sandbox timeout (RC-2 fix) provides defense-in-depth against all runaway commands. The prompt guardrails complement the hard enforcement with soft guidance. The completion signal verification catches any remaining state corruption.
recommended_approach.key_insight: The push failure was not a bug in the gateway's diff logic — the diff correctly identified files that the refine phase cannot modify. The bug is in the orchestrator's failure to ensure the remote branch is up-to-date before spawning a new phase agent. Fixing the precondition (sync) is safer than weakening the check (scoped diff).
recommended_approach.option_f_rationale: Option F (Shell Command Timeout Wrapper) is CRITICAL, not optional. The analysis recommended E+F as a defense-in-depth pair: prompt guardrails (soft) + command timeout (hard). Without Option F, the only protection against runaway commands is the prompt guardrail, which the model can ignore (risk analyst assessed 'medium' likelihood). The 22-minute runaway grep consumed $8+ in compute and left the pipeline in an ambiguous state. A system-level timeout is the only way to guarantee bounded resource consumption regardless of model behavior.
rollout_order: 1. Prompt guardrails (sandbox/.claude/rules/environment.md) — immediate, zero-risk, addresses most common agent behavior
2. Gateway push-target enforcement — small change, prevents wrong-branch push, add killswitch
3. Pre-phase worktree sync — orchestrator change, addresses the core push failure root cause
4. Sandbox per-command timeout wrapper — requires investigation of Claude Code's subprocess path, then implementation
5. Completion signal branch verification — orchestrator change, catches remaining state corruption

architecture_decisions.decision: Fix the precondition (sync), not the check (diff)
architecture_decisions.rationale: The gateway's get_changed_files_in_push() uses a two-dot diff (origin/{branch}..HEAD) that is security-conservative — it shows exactly what the push would change on the remote. Weakening this to a scoped diff could introduce security gaps. Instead, ensure the precondition is met: the remote branch tip should be up-to-date with prior phases' commits before the new phase agent starts.

architecture_decisions.decision: Enforce push-target at the gateway, not the orchestrator
architecture_decisions.rationale: The gateway is the security enforcement boundary for all git operations. Adding push-target validation there ensures the check cannot be bypassed. The completion signal verification on the orchestrator side is defense-in-depth.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use a system-level per-command timeout independent of Claude Code's Bash tool timeout
architecture_decisions.rationale: Claude Code's Bash tool has a per-call timeout parameter, but it is model-controlled — the model can set it up to 600000ms (10 min). A system-level timeout provides a hard ceiling that cannot be overridden by the model. The implementation must cover Claude Code's actual subprocess invocation path, which uses direct subprocess execution (not login shells).

architecture_decisions.decision: Default timeout of 120 seconds, not 300 seconds
architecture_decisions.rationale: 120 seconds aligns with Claude Code's own default Bash timeout (120000ms). Most legitimate shell commands (file operations, git, grep within repos, single test files) complete well within 2 minutes. Test suites and builds that need longer can use explicit overrides. This catches runaway commands sooner than a 5-minute timeout would.

architecture_decisions.decision: Layer soft guardrails (prompt) with hard guardrails (timeout, gateway enforcement)
architecture_decisions.rationale: Prompt guardrails reduce the frequency of problems but cannot eliminate them. Hard guardrails (timeout kills, gateway rejection) provide the safety net. Both layers are needed: the prompt reduces disruption (fewer timeouts), while the hard enforcement prevents catastrophic outcomes (26-minute hangs, wrong-branch state corruption).

architecture_decisions.decision: Push-target enforcement only in pipeline mode with killswitch
architecture_decisions.rationale: When agents run outside the SDLC pipeline, they may legitimately push to various branches. Push-target enforcement only activates when session has both pipeline_id and assigned_branch set. The PUSH_TARGET_ENFORCEMENT env var provides instant rollback without code deploy.

architecture_decisions.decision: Completion signal verification is hard-block when commit SHA provided, skip when None
architecture_decisions.rationale: The risk analyst correctly identified that warning-only verification allows the pipeline to continue with stale state — the same outcome as the original incident. When an agent provides a commit SHA, that SHA must be on the expected branch. If the agent pushes to the wrong branch, the commit won't be found and the signal is rejected. When no commit is provided, some phases legitimately complete without pushing, so the check is skipped.

architecture_decisions.decision: Pre-phase push checks prior phase status before pushing accumulated commits
architecture_decisions.rationale: If the prior agent crashed mid-work, its local commits may be incomplete or broken. Pushing these to remote makes them permanent. The sync function should check whether the prior phase completed successfully: push only on success, discard on failure/crash.

tasks.description: Investigate and document Claude Code's Bash tool shell invocation path in the sandbox

tasks.detail: Based on the investigation in task-timeout-1, implement the timeout wrapper using the approach that covers Claude Code's actual invocation path. (b) If Claude Code uses a specific shell binary: replace or wrap that binary with a timeout-enforcing wrapper. The agent may have pushed to a different branch.' If found, accept normally. When commit is None, skip the verification entirely (some phases may legitimately complete without committing). Compare against phase_start_sha to detect no-new-commits scenario and log a warning (but don't block).
acceptance_criteria: Completion with commit SHA on expected branch: accepted
Completion with commit SHA NOT on expected branch: rejected with 409 and descriptive error
Completion with commit=None: accepted without branch check
Warning logged when no new commits since phase_start_sha (branch tip unchanged)
Branch fetch failure does not block the signal (best-effort, log warning)

risks.risk: Per-command timeout wrapper may not activate depending on Claude Code's shell invocation path
risks.mitigation: Dedicated investigation task (task-timeout-1) before implementation. Research shows Claude Code uses subprocess.Popen (not login shells), so /etc/profile.d/ is NOT viable. Implementation must use an approach that covers the actual invocation path. BASH_ENV, shell binary wrapping, or process monitoring are the candidates.
risks.human_review_reason: The timeout implementation approach needs validation against Claude Code's actual behavior. The implementer must test the chosen approach in the sandbox before committing.

risks.risk: Pre-phase push may push incomplete work from crashed prior agents
risks.mitigation: Check prior phase's agent execution status before pushing. Only push on successful completion; discard on failure/crash.

risks.risk: Push-target refspec parsing has diverse edge cases that may cause false rejections
risks.mitigation: Use existing extract_branch_from_refspec() which already handles common formats. Comprehensive test coverage for all push syntaxes. PUSH_TARGET_ENFORCEMENT killswitch for instant rollback.

risks.risk: Push-target enforcement may block auto-commit and push_worktree_branch() temporary sessions
risks.mitigation: Explicitly verify both temporary session paths. Either set assigned_branch on temporary sessions or exempt them from the check. Integration test covering the full auto-commit flow with enforcement enabled.
risks.human_review_reason: Auto-commit is a critical safety net. Blocking it silently would cause data loss.

risks.risk: Per-command timeout may kill legitimate long-running test suites and builds
risks.mitigation: Default 120s is sufficient for most commands. Agents can use Claude Code's per-call timeout parameter for known-long operations. BASH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT env var allows per-container override.

risks.risk: Push-target enforcement killswitch bug blocks ALL pipeline pushes
risks.mitigation: PUSH_TARGET_ENFORCEMENT env var defaults to true but can be set to false for instant rollback. Staged deployment: enable with logging first, then enable blocking.

open_questions_resolved.question: When _sync_worktree_with_remote() encounters local-ahead state and the push fails, should it attempt to force-push?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: No force-push. Log and continue. Also check prior phase status: only push on successful completion, discard on failure. Force-push risks losing concurrent work.

open_questions_resolved.question: What per-command timeout value balances safety and usability?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: 120 seconds (not 300s). Aligns with Claude Code's own default. Catches runaway commands sooner while being sufficient for most legitimate operations.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should push-target enforcement block the push (403) or warn and allow it?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Hard block (403). A warning defeats the purpose. Add PUSH_TARGET_ENFORCEMENT killswitch for rollback.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should prompt guardrails go in global CLAUDE.md or sandbox-specific rules?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Sandbox-specific rules (sandbox/.claude/rules/environment.md). The global CLAUDE.md is for user-facing instructions; the sandbox rules are for enforcement-level guidance.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should completion signal verification be a warning or hard block?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Hard block when commit SHA is provided (HTTP 409). Skip check when commit is None. This is strict-when-relevant, permissive-when-appropriate.
